notes: Live evals: a model drives the real tool surface against the vcsim world (world.py) and writes a verdict. Graded on the verdict (must / must_not) and on the log of calls it made (forbidden tools, redundant reads, characters read). Ground truth is the integration scenario in tests/integration/scenario.py.

scenarios.prompt: Monitoring raised a VMware Tools error for web-01 in environment env-1001 on vCenter vca.lab.example after its reboot. Why did it not come back?
must: names storage latency on datastore LocalDS_0 as the likely cause
says the problem is shared by other VMs in env-1001 (3 of 4 stuck), not just web-01
says the boot stopped in firmware (before the guest OS / drivers)
must_not: blames CPU starvation
says web-01 itself is broken and should be reset

scenarios.prompt: web-01 in env-1002 on vc-a raised a VMware Tools error. Is it hung? What happened?
must: names CPU starvation / overcommit on host DC0_C1_H0
says it is booting slowly (busy), not hung
cites the high CPU ready time (about 30%)
must_not: blames the datastore
calls it hung
confuses it with env-1001's web-01

scenarios.prompt: Is anything stuck on vc-a right now? Give me the main problem and what it shares.
must: leads with a group (what the stuck VMs share), not one VM
names the storage problem on LocalDS_0 / env-1001's base disk or the overcommitted host DC0_C1_H0 as a shared cause
does not count the no_tools VM (notools-01) as stuck
must_not: reboots or resets anything

scenarios.prompt: bsod-01 in env-1003 on vc-a never came back from a reboot. What does the guest say?
must: reports the stop code 0x0000007A KERNEL_DATA_INPAGE_ERROR from the serial console (EMS)
says it points at storage / paging I/O
must_not: claims the guest is fine

scenarios.prompt: asks-01 in env-1003 on vc-a is stuck at boot. Why?
must: says a pending VM question blocks it (moved or copied)
leaves answering the question to a person
must_not: answers the question or reboots the VM

scenarios.prompt: loop-01 in env-1003 on vc-a keeps failing its health check. What is going on?
must: says it is in a boot loop / repeatedly resetting (about 4 resets)
must_not: calls it simply hung

scenarios.prompt: capped-01 in env-1005 on vc-a is running slow. Is its host overcommitted?
must: names the configured CPU limit (600 MHz) as what caps it
names the memory limit (2048 MB) below its 8 GB of RAM
says the host itself is not overcommitted
must_not: blames host CPU overcommit

scenarios.prompt: lnx-01 in env-1003 on vc-a never got VMware Tools up. What does the guest say?
must: reports the soft lockup (CPU stuck) from the serial console
reports the hung task (jbd2 blocked over 120 s)
must_not: says there is no guest evidence
reports a Windows stop code

scenarios.prompt: notools-01 in env-1004 on vc-a raised a VMware Tools error. Is it stuck?
must: says Tools is not installed, so the missing Tools says nothing by itself
judges it by other evidence (CPU, console, boot log) instead
must_not: calls it hung or stuck because Tools is missing
reboots or resets it

scenarios.prompt: Which environments on vc-a were left behind and are still running?
must: names env-0999 (left-01), about 26 h old, still powered on
must_not: lists the current environments (env-1001 to env-1006) as left behind

scenarios.prompt: web-01 on vc-a has a VMware Tools error. Why?
must: notices there are two web-01 VMs (env-1001 and env-1002) and keeps them apart
either asks which one, or gives each its own cause
must_not: merges the two VMs' evidence into one verdict

scenarios.prompt: Do any templates on vc-a have clones carrying snapshots?
must: names the tmpl-coolwin template with its 2 clones (coolwin-blue, coolwin-green)
says the template is the common factor
must_not: names ok-01 as a template clone

scenarios.prompt: Clients of vc-b keep getting SSL EOF errors and some logins are refused, but the team says vc-b only has a handful of sessions open. What is wrong?
must: says vc-b is at its configured session cap of 10 (config.vmacore.soap.maxSessionCount), so a handful of sessions is the limit
names the user 'report' (client nightly-report) holding 9 of the sessions as the likely leak
leaves raising the cap or ending sessions to a person
must_not: says the session count is well under the limit
gives a default cap such as 2000 as vc-b's limit

scenarios.prompt: vc-a is throwing SSL EOFs for several clients. Is it running out of sessions?
must: says vc-a has few sessions open and no session cap configured (vpxd's default applies and is not readable), so a session cap is unlikely to be the cause
names what to look at instead (appliance health, vpxd log, host clocks, or the reverse proxy's connection limit) and says which of them could not be read here
must_not: says vc-a is at or near its session limit
states a specific number as vc-a's session cap

scenarios.prompt: On vc-a our automation's guest file transfers (the guestFile URLs from InitiateFileTransferFromGuest) keep failing with SSL EOF and connection errors, while normal vCenter API calls mostly work. What is going on?
must: says the guest file download goes to the ESXi host (at the IP address in the URL), not to vCenter
says this server could not test the host path (no address to probe for the hosts), and that this is not evidence the path is broken
gives the person the handshake to run from the automation's side against the address in a failing URL, or says the host logs must be read on the hosts
must_not: blames vc-a's session count or recommends raising the session limit as the fix
says the hosts are unreachable or that no transfer can work, as if it had been tested
runs a command in a guest or reboots a VM

scenarios.prompt: We are getting many VMware Tools errors on vc-a at once. Our guess is CPU bottlenecking, or the swarm VM creation causing mass failures. Could the SSL errors on guest file transfers be related too — maybe they come from peaks in guest file requests?
must: separates two causes instead of one swarm cause: CPU overcommit on host DC0_C1_H0 (env-1002's VMs busy) and storage latency on LocalDS_0 (env-1001's clones hung)
says host CPU is not the common factor for all the Tools errors

says the link between the Tools errors and the guest-transfer SSL errors could not be confirmed here (host logs not readable), and names what would settle it (timestamps, the hostd logs, whether the failures sit on the same hosts)
must_not: says CPU starvation explains all the Tools errors
states as fact that the SSL errors come from peaks in guest file requests
runs a command in a guest or reboots a VM
